\chapter{Requirement Analysis}

The objective of the requirement analysis is to establish clear expectations of the PCMA's joint design for the purposes of concept generation and development.

\section{Identification of Stakeholders}

The first step in the requirement analysis process is to identify stakeholders from the operational and support life cycle phases of the project. Stakeholders will be classified into the following categories, as defined below:
\begin{itemize}
	\item Primary stakeholders directly interact with the system while it is in operation.
	\item Secondary stakeholders contribute to the development and functioning of the system.
	\item Indirect stakeholders rely on or are affected by the system, but do not interact with the system directly.
\end{itemize}
The stakeholders relevant to the project are defined in Table~\ref{tab:SID table} below.

\section{Technical Performance Measures}

This section defines the technical performance measures (TPMs) which will be used to determine how well the joint design (NSoI) performs the required functions\footnote{TPMs are measurable and unambiguous parameters that can be influenced by designing the joint}. The TPMs, listed in Table~\ref{tab:TPMs}, were derived from the results obtained from the generalised error-propagation model. 

\begin{table}[H]
	\centering
	\caption{Joint Technical Performance Measures}
	\label{tab:TPMs}
	\begin{tabular}{|l|l|l|l|}
		\hline
		\textbf{TPM ID} & \textbf{Related FR} & \textbf{Description} & \textbf{Target Value} \\\hline
		TPM\_01 & FR\_01, FR\_05 & Operational articulation angle & \SI{90}{\degree} \\\hline
		TPM\_02 & FR\_01, FR\_05 & Run-out tolerance & \SI{1e-3}{rad} \\\hline
		TPM\_03 & FR\_02 & Holding torque & \SI{7.725}{Nm} \\\hline
		TPM\_04 & FR\_03, FR\_04 & Encoder resolution & \SI{9}{bits} \\\hline
		TPM\_05 & FR\_01, FR\_02, FR\_05 & Joint life cycle & \num{e6} life cycles \\\hline
	\end{tabular}
\end{table}

Each target value is derived from the generalised D-H error propagation model and static loading requirements. The following subsections, Section 3.4.1 to 3.4.5, provide detailed derivations, calculations, and mechanical justifications for TPM\_01 TO TPM\_05, respectively.

\subsection{TPM\_01: Operational Articulation Angle}

The \SI{90}{\degree} articulation TPM is derived from the D-H kinematic model to ensure that the joint mechanism provides the minimum range motion needed to cover all measurement coordinates within the PCMA working volume. This target value is a baseline of the D-H transformation chain and it guarentees that the complete kinematic path is fulfilled without restricting the arm's reach.

\subsection{TPM\_02: Run-Out Tolerance}

Minute bearing play and shaft imperfections can cause the joint to wobble during rotation. If this wobble is not bounded, it can introduce unintentional spatial drift at the probe tip. TPM\_02 ensures that the axis maintains alignment and measurement stability.

The TPM is reliant on two parameters. One being an arbitrarily chosen to be joint diameter, $d_{joint}=\SI{20}{mm}$, to match commercially available bearings. The second being, the allowable radial bearing deflection defined under ISO 492:2014 as $\delta r_{bearing}=\SI{0.01}{mm}$ \citep{ISO492:2014}. This deflection represents the standard manufacturer precision tolerance for radial internal clearance and run-out. These two parameters are then used to calculate the runout tolerance as shown in Equation~\ref{eq:TPM_02}.

\begin{equation}\label{eq:TPM_02}
	\begin{aligned}
		\Theta_{\text{runout}} &= \frac{\delta r_{\text{bearing}}}{\left(\frac{d_{\text{joint}}}{2}\right)} \\
		&= \frac{0.010}{\left(\frac{20}{2}\right)} \\
		&= \SI{1e-3}{rad}
	\end{aligned}
\end{equation}

By limiting the run-out tolerance, it is ensured that the joint rotation will only track single-axis motion without off-axis tilt, which will preserve D-H kinematic model integrity and minimise spatial errors at the probe tip.

\subsection{TPM\_03: Holding Torque}

If the position-holding mechanism is uable to produce a sufficient static holding torque, the weight of the distal links can cause the arm to slip. By establishing TPM\_03, the joint is guaranteed to secure and maintain its angular position under a maximum gravity-induced cantilever moment without unexpected drift.

Figure~\ref{fig:whatsapp-image-2026-10-05-at-15} depicts the freebody diagram used to calculate the holding torque.

\begin{figure}[H]
	\centering
	\includegraphics[width=0.7\linewidth]{"../../../../../../../../../Downloads/WhatsApp Image 2026-10-05 at 15.19.12"}
	\caption{FBD of one of the Faro QuantumX links}
	\label{fig:whatsapp-image-2026-10-05-at-15}
\end{figure}

From the user manual \citep{Faro:2024}, the mass of the link is \SI{1.5}{kg}, and the distance from the center of the link to the center of the joint is \SI{0.35}{m}. The holding torque was determined in Equation~\ref{eq:holding_torque}, with a safety factor of 1.5 applied:

\begin{equation}
	\label{eq:holding_torque}
	\begin{split}
		T &= SF\cdot m\cdot g\cdot l\\
		&= (1.5)(1.5)(9.81)(0.35) \\
		&= \SI{7.725}{Nm}
	\end{split}
\end{equation}

By achieving this holding torque, the position-holding mechanism will be able to successfully support the distal links when the mechanism is actuated.

\subsection{TPM\_04: Encoder Resolution}

Accurate spatial measurement in a PCMA depends on the ability of each joint's rotary encoder to digitise small angular displacements. If the optical encoder resolution is too coarse, quantisation error is emphasised, which prevents the system from meeting single-joint angular precision targets. Establishing TPM\_04 ensures that the chosen encoder resolution provides sufficient quantisation to keep measurement error minimised.

The required encoder resolution is calculated using the worse-case uncertainty established under Section 2.2, specifically $\sigma_{\theta,\text{required}}=\SI{1.957e-5}{rad}$. This value comes from the D-H kinematic error propagation derivations, applied across a full rotational range of \SI{360}{\degree}.
